headline: High-risk compliance and cascading-error concerns: ComfyUI can feed media into social-auto-upload, creating default-path publication and policy mismatch risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP/browser bridge, while social-auto-upload is CLI/headless and does not read filesystems by default. The only plausible bridge is manual handoff of generated media or metadata, so prompt-injection-style hijack is limited and not default. Interaction is inferred from both profiles, not directly documented.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ComfyUI outputs into social-auto-upload inputs, attacker-controlled text embedded in filenames/captions can influence upload metadata.
IF either agent is wrapped by a shared script that parses generated prompts as commands, injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep a human review step for captions, titles, and filenames before upload.
Use a fixed export folder with sanitized filenames only.
Disable any wrapper that interprets generated text as shell or CLI flags.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between generation and upload stages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are open-source and appear local-first: ComfyUI works fully offline, and social-auto-upload is headless CLI with broad network egress only for uploads. No shared filesystem or authenticated workspace is documented, so leakage is not a default pathway. The main risk is manual transfer of sensitive media/account data into the uploader.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive images or videos into social-auto-upload's input files, those assets may be transmitted to external platforms.
IF ComfyUI outputs contain embedded secrets in metadata and are copied into the uploader, those secrets can leak.
mitigations: Strip metadata from generated media before upload.
Use a dedicated non-sensitive test account for uploads.
Review the exact files queued for upload before starting.
Store account files separately from generated media.
requires-engineering: add automatic redaction of metadata and secrets.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and both lack shared mutable resource scopes in the profiles. ComfyUI is offline and social-auto-upload is headless CLI, but without write or coordination primitives there is no plausible concurrent-write conflict. This pathway is blocked by the documented capabilities.
conditions: IF either profile is extended with filesystem write access to the same directory, conflict risk becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator adds locking-free shared state, concurrent mutation could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared directories.
Avoid running them under a shared mutable workspace.
Use separate output folders per agent.
requires-engineering: add file locks if write access is later introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can generate images/videos that social-auto-upload may treat as ready-to-publish content, so B can act on A's output with limited verification. The uploader's broad network egress makes downstream publication plausible, and the pair lacks a documented verification gate. This is an inferred interaction from both profiles, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are passed directly into social-auto-upload's queue, B may publish unreviewed or incorrect media.
IF captions or account targets are derived from A's outputs without validation, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require manual approval before upload.
Preview the exact post payload in social-auto-upload.
Use a staging account for dry runs.
Add a checklist for title, tags, and destination account.
requires-engineering: insert a validation step between generation and upload.

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI touches generated media, workflows, and model artifacts, while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads to social platforms. If regulated or personal media is generated in one tool and uploaded by the other, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No DPA, residency, or retention controls are documented, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF the workflow includes EU personal data or PHI in generated media, compliance review is required before upload.
IF account data and media are retained under different policies, deletion/export obligations may be inconsistent.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the generation/upload pipeline.
Use separate accounts for personal and production content.
Document retention periods for both tools.
Review platform terms before publishing.
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware retention and deletion handling.
